properties.name: A composed analysis across a family's designs writes what it finds at the seams back as cross-design gaps the hub's loop shows: an interface declared on one side only, a requirement sent down and never accepted, a relation unstated, one thing named twice
properties.statement:
When a hub's designs are assembled for analysis (compose_and_analyse locally, or the host for hosted designs), the findings that belong to the seams rather than to one design are recorded as gaps on the hub, each naming the designs and nodes involved: an Interface one side provides and no other consumes, or consumes with no provider; a requirement sent down to a part (send_to_design) that the part has not accepted; a member whose relation to the hub is unstated; one fact held in two designs (a near-duplicate above the stated threshold, as a candidate); a quantity within limits in each design and over them in the whole, where units allow the roll-up. loop_status on the hub lists them; detect-and-ask puts them to the person; acknowledging one records why. Run on ask, and on a schedule where a host holds the designs.
Anthony, 2026-10-10: "'assembled when asked' ... might even lead to gap discovery where two designs don't 'interface' properly." He kept option (c) of dec:idea-two-designs-are-compared-on-one-topic-on-demand. Kept beside it: a seam gap needs a declared seam; two designs that never declared how they meet yield "nothing links them" (the members_unlinked finding), not an interface fault, so the first gap such a pass raises is usually that one.
